subject: Cloud Computing
title: Block Storage: Virtual Hard Drives
description: A 60-second lesson on Block Storage: Virtual Hard Drives.

hook.text: Your cloud server needs a hard drive. Block storage provides one — virtual, fast, and resizable on demand.

buildup.text: Block storage splits data into fixed-size chunks called blocks. The operating system manages them like a local disk.

discovery.text: AWS EBS, Azure Managed Disks, and GCP Persistent Disks are block storage. They attach directly to virtual machines.

twist.text: Block storage is tied to one server at a time. Sharing it across multiple machines requires a file system on top.

climax.text: Databases love block storage. Low latency and consistent performance make it ideal for transactional workloads.

punchline.text: Block storage is your cloud hard drive. Fast, local, dedicated.

quiz.question: Why do databases commonly use block storage?
options: It offers low latency and consistent performance for transactional workloads
Block storage is the only type that can store structured data
Databases cannot run on object or file storage

details.summary: Block storage provides raw storage volumes that attach to virtual machines like physical hard drives. Data is divided into fixed-size blocks for fast random access. It is essential for databases, operating systems, and applications needing low-latency disk I/O.
details.whyItMatters: Block storage powers the disks behind every virtual machine and most cloud databases. Choosing the right volume type directly affects application performance and cost.
takeaways: Provides raw volumes that attach to virtual machines
Optimized for low-latency random read and write access
Essential for databases and operating system disks

faq.question: What are IOPS and why do they matter?
faq.answer: IOPS stands for input/output operations per second, measuring how many read and write operations a volume can handle. Database workloads require high IOPS. Cloud providers offer volume types optimized for IOPS, throughput, or cost.

faq.question: How does block storage differ from object storage?
faq.answer: Block storage provides low-latency access for operating systems and databases but is limited to the region and availability zone. Object storage is accessed via HTTP, scales globally, and is cheaper but too slow for database workloads.
